answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying influence to scarce, slowly earned credentials instead of cheap new identities. Anyone can spin up a thousand wallets, but only accounts that have completed attested work over time gain voting weight and payouts. The credential is like a pigment drawn from juniper and locked in quartz: costly to produce, easy to verify, and hard to fake at scale. That cost makes mass impersonation unprofitable, so the network can trust reputation more than raw headcount.
